decisions.reason: As a prominently launched new-generation core printer on the home page, it reflects high sunk development costs, public commitment and clear fit with the firm's main marking systems business.

This software module extends the firm's established coding offer into variable-data printing and digitalization, and repeated website mentions make it easier for management to justify continued support despite any slow uptake.

Because this coder is close to the core product line and broadens coverage for difficult non-absorbent surfaces, management would likely persist with it and view any weaker results as a temporary market-development issue.

Although publicly introduced as a successor app, it is more peripheral to the firm's machinery-centered offering and likely involves lower sunk costs, so management has less reason to escalate commitment if traction is limited.

An inline code verification system is highly aligned with the firm's stated move toward serialization and end-to-end traceability, which increases strategic commitment even if early market signals were modest.
Home-page promotion and strong complementarity with installed printers and common system operation create both visible commitment and ecosystem value, favoring continuation.
